authentication.authority: The configured default-home Synapse verifies passwords, revocation and token expiry. This service is not an OIDC issuer.

sessionResponse.access_token: REDACTED: never a public configuration field
sessionResponse.device_id: one distinct Matrix device per client login
sessionResponse.expires_in_ms: optional Matrix-provided expiry; absence does not assert a lifetime

logout.semantics: Revoke only this Matrix client device session; repeated logout is successful. Legacy synthetic demo service credentials remain local-only logout.

authentication.csrf: No ambient cookie credentials; JSON mutations and exact configured Origin checks. Cross-origin requests require an explicit allowlist.

oidc.upgradeCandidate: Matrix Authentication Service or Synapse native OIDC; issuer/subject binding must be proven, never inferred from display name or email

discovery.credentials: omit: public discovery must not carry passwords, Authorization, cookies or node credentials
discovery.legacy: Without explicit public Core URL, standalone discovery returns home.coreUrl=null and credentials.coreOrigin=null; resolve the Core only to the origin from which discovery was fetched. Central mode requires explicit public URLs. Existing /api/bootstrap fields remain compatible.

deployment.config: core-config.json identity: { mode: central|standalone, coreUrl, matrixUrl, clientOrigins: [exact origins] }
persistentState: identity-config.json: immutable authority ID and Matrix server name, selected public URLs and client origins
accounts.sqlite: unique Matrix ID to immutable subject mapping
existing Matrix database, signing key and node-credentials.sqlite
deployment.defaultHome: The configured setup.serverName is the default home. It cannot be repointed to a different Matrix server name on restart.
deployment.clientOrigins: HTTPS origins, or HTTP loopback origins for local verification. No wildcard, null, credentials, query or path. Core origin is allowed automatically.
deployment.serverInit: A dedicated central-init script configures the identity section after ordinary server-init; existing server-init and CLI remain compatible.

credentialRules: Pin a trusted discovery source before entering credentials. A user-added collaboration URL is untrusted and gets credential-free discovery only.
Passwords go only to the pinned home Core login/register endpoints. Matrix access tokens go only to the pinned home Core /api endpoints or home Matrix /_matrix/client and /_matrix/media endpoints.
Never follow credential-bearing redirects. A remote bootstrap response cannot change the home of a stored session.
No ordinary home token is accepted as a node, remote Core or deployment management credential. Federated room participation preserves the complete original Matrix ID.
Remote product APIs need a separately negotiated target-specific proof/session. This slice issues no remote credentials.

compatibility.existingAccounts: Migrate mapping additively in accounts.sqlite; preserve Matrix IDs, service tokens, room history, Bot owner IDs and node credentials. Import an unregistered local Matrix identity only after successful password proof at its actual home.
compatibility.foreignAccounts: Do not bind or create shadow accounts by matching localpart, display name or email. Cross-home identity linking is not implemented.
compatibility.recovery: Recover the same Matrix account through existing homeserver/operator recovery, then authenticate again. Restore the identity config, accounts database and Matrix state together to preserve subjects. No email recovery service or automatic homeserver migration is claimed.
compatibility.disableAndExpiry: Matrix remains the revocation/expiry authority. Rejected whoami invalidates Core access. A disabled local account must not be reactivated by login. Direct Matrix deactivation uses homeserver administration, independently authorized.
compatibility.bots: Keep the exact Bot Matrix ID and owner Matrix ID. Map owner subjects additively; keep node credentials and service sessions distinct from human client sessions.
compatibility.admin: Central login does not confer per-server deployment administration. Independent admin API and federation gate are owned by the parallel server slice.

independentOriginBrowser.scope: real Chromium test page using normal Core/Synapse APIs; registration/login, pinned-home requests, forbidden-origin preflight, attachment upload/retry/full/range reads; not the parallel final TS UI

verification.federatedRoom: parallel server slice; not verified here

details: CORS permits X-Upload-Id required by actual attachment uploads and exposes response metadata
No product SDK: frontend owns the TS transport; tests/helpers/home-session.mjs is verification-only
Legacy standalone null Core URL resolves against trusted discovery origin; API session home may keep coreUrl=null until the client normalizes it
A legacy reverse proxy with no configured publicUrl may preserve HTTPS Host for same-origin requests
